data.title: Events with heart and a personal touch.
data.intro: Celebration Studio is a small party-planning and styling studio working around Port Alder and the Wren Valley, and wherever else a good table can be set.

children.text: We started the studio because we love the moment when a room fills with people who are glad to be there. Our work is warm, practical and a little bit playful, and we take on a limited number of celebrations each season so that every host gets our full attention.

Most of what we plan happens outdoors or in garden rooms, with long tables, plenty of flowers and a lot of candlelight. Whether the gathering is for eight people or eighty, the approach is the same: understand what matters, build a plan that holds, then take care of the details.
How we work

We begin with a conversation, not a form. We learn about your guests and the day you imagine, then propose a design, a budget and a plan. We handle suppliers, timelines and guest questions, and stay close until the last song.
We answer every message personally, usually within two working days. Names, places and prices on this site are fictional sample content.

data.title: Booking notes
data.intro: A few things that help every celebration run smoothly.

children.text: Booking
An enquiry is not a booking. We reply by email, talk through your plans and, if we are a good fit, confirm with a short written agreement and a deposit.
Payments
Fees are paid in instalments, with the balance due before the celebration. Supplier payments are made by you directly unless we have agreed otherwise in writing.
Changes
Plans change. If you need to move your date or guest count, tell us as early as you can and we will do everything possible to protect your suppliers and deposits.

data.title: Styling & Design
data.summary: Tables, flowers, colour and light, designed around your guests and your sense of fun.
data.best_for: Hosts who have the date and want it to look wonderful
data.includes:
Mood board and colour story
Table plan and place-setting design
Florals, candles and linens sourced and set
Signage, menus and place cards
Set-up and clear-down on the day

children.text: Styling is where a celebration starts to feel like yours. We begin with a short conversation about the people coming, the place and the mood you have in mind, then turn it into a colour story, a table design and a shopping list of flowers, linens and little details.
What it looks like

Think a long table with pink linen and brass candlesticks, a loose centrepiece of seasonal flowers, hand-lettered menus and a place card for every guest. We bring everything, set it, light it and photograph it for you before the first guest arrives.
Styling can stand alone or sit inside a fuller planning package. Either way you get a clear proposal with a fixed price before anything is ordered.

data.title: Planning & Coordination
data.summary: A steady hand for the venue, suppliers, guest list and timeline, so you can enjoy your own party.
data.best_for: Hosts who would rather not manage ten suppliers at once
data.includes:
Planning call and shared checklist
Venue shortlist and site visits
Supplier introductions and bookings
Budget and payment calendar
Guest communication and RSVPs
On-the-day coordination from set-up to last song

children.text: Good planning is mostly quiet: a checklist that is always up to date, a budget with no surprises and a person to call when something changes. We handle the thinking so that your attention stays on the people you are celebrating.
How we work

We find and brief the venue, caterer, florist, baker and musicians, keep every date and payment in one shared timeline, and manage guest questions as they arrive. On the day we run the schedule and look after suppliers, so you are never the one carrying the cake.
Choose full planning from the first idea, or coordination only for the final weeks. We will suggest the lighter option if it is all you need.

data.title: Unique Celebrations
data.summary: Milestone birthdays, anniversaries and one-of-a-kind gatherings, built from scratch around a story.
data.best_for: Milestones that deserve a one-off idea
data.includes:
Concept development workshop
Custom design for the whole setting
Bespoke installations, lighting and signage
Programme of moments: toasts, surprises, music
Full planning and coordination
Photographer and florist liaison

children.text: Some days are not on any template. A thirtieth with a neon sign and four hundred dahlias, a retirement lunch among the olive trees, a surprise anniversary for a couple who say they hate surprises. We start from the story and design everything to fit.
How it works

We hold a short concept workshop, then bring you a design, a programme for the day and a quote. Because every celebration is different, pricing is quoted individually once we know the guest count, place and scale.

data.title: Floral & Balloon Installations
data.summary: Balloon arches, flower walls and hanging garlands made to fill a doorway, backdrop or whole room.
data.best_for: Parties that want one big, joyful focal point
data.includes:
Design sketch and colour match
Balloon, foliage and flower build
Delivery, installation and removal
Backdrop panels and stands
Fresh-flower top-ups on request

children.text: An installation is the photograph everyone takes first. We build arches, columns and backdrops in blush, gold and cream, wrapped in eucalyptus or olive and finished with fresh flowers where the season allows.
Pieces are made in our workshop, installed on site and taken away afterwards, so there is nothing to dispose of at the end of the night.

data.title: Private Dinners & Tables
data.summary: Seated dinners for twelve to sixty: tables, tableware, menus and service for an evening to remember.
data.best_for: Anniversaries, family dinners and milestone suppers
data.includes:
Table design and hire of linens, glassware and candles
Menu planning with local caterers
Seating plan and place cards
Service staff for the evening
Set-up and clear-down

children.text: A long table with the right people around it is hard to beat. We plan the evening end to end: the setting, the menu, the order of the night and the small details that make guests linger.
We work in gardens, terraces, restaurants' private rooms and at home. Tell us the number of guests and the space and we will propose a layout and a price.

data.title: Poppy's Garden Birthday
data.summary: A long table under the roses with pink linen, dahlias and a neon sign above the lawn.

gallery.caption: A tall arrangement of dahlias and ranunculus on a stone urn.
Coupe glasses and fluted votives along the table.
A hand-bent neon sign lit once the sun went down.
A lettered card at every place.

children.text: Poppy turned thirty-five and asked for a lunch that felt like a garden party in a magazine, with her closest friends and no schedule. Marlow Court gave us a sheltered terrace, a very long table and the rose-covered wall behind it.

We dressed the table in soft pink linen and rattan chargers, set brass cutlery and ribbed votives between the plates and built a loose centrepiece in coral, peach and butter-yellow. A neon sign in warm white was hung on the wall for the evening.
What we planned
Styling and design, supplier booking, the menu with the caterer, the birthday cake and the order of the afternoon, from the first prosecco to the last candle.

data.title: Twenty-Five Years, One Long Table
data.place: The Orangery at Hallam House, Port Alder
data.summary: A silver anniversary dinner with peonies, gold candlesticks and the whole family at one table.

gallery.caption: Tall blush candles in brass holders at the head of the table.
Linen napkins folded over plates, with sprigs of olive.
Evening light through the arches of the orangery.

children.text: Ana and Tomas had been married for twenty-five years and wanted to thank the people who had been there for all of them. The Orangery at Hallam House holds forty-six at a single table, which was exactly the point.

A bowl of peonies, ranunculus and wild mimosa sat in the middle on a brass pedestal, with candles in graduated heights down the table. Each guest found a handwritten card with a memory from the couple.
What we planned
Table design and hire, the menu and wine, the seating plan and a short programme of toasts, finishing with a surprise slide show from the children.

data.title: Blush & Gold Baby Shower
data.summary: A sunlit afternoon of balloons, pale flowers and a three-tier cake for a first baby.

gallery.caption: Candles and balloon garlands against a blush backdrop.
Garden roses in a speckled ceramic vase.
A floral cake on a brass stand.
Coupes and candles on the dessert table.

children.text: Lena wanted a baby shower that was calm, pretty and not too sweet. We took a blush-and-gold palette, kept the balloons to a single airy arch and added plenty of foliage so it felt like a garden.
Guests were seated at two tables rather than in rows, with games kept to one short round and a long tea service in the middle of the afternoon.
What we planned
Installation, table styling, the cake, catering and the guest flow, including a quiet corner for the mother-to-be.

data.title: Sunset Supper on the Terrace
data.summary: Lanterns, linen and a long table above the sea for eighteen friends.

gallery.caption: The lounge corner lit for the after-dinner hour.
Candlelight along the table as the light faded.
Arches and olive trees at the edge of the terrace.

children.text: The brief from Imogen was an evening that felt like the last night of the summer. Seacliff Terrace looks west over the water, so we laid one table facing the sunset and left the other end open for a lounge.
We lit the evening with brass lanterns and low candles, kept the flowers wild and low so nobody had to look around them, and moved the whole party to the sofas for coffee when the sky turned pink.
What we planned
Table design, catering liaison, lighting and the evening's order, with a quiet change of scene after dinner.

data.title: Hollis Turns Forty
data.summary: A neon-lit barn party with velvet chairs, balloons and a very long dance floor.

gallery.caption: A blush and gold balloon arch at the barn door.
Dusty-rose velvet chairs around the dinner tables.
Pink linen and rattan chargers on the head table.

children.text: Hollis wanted a party that felt like a dinner and a disco at once. In Linden Barn we split the room: long tables with velvet chairs at one end, a neon wall and open floor at the other.
The balloon arch at the entrance was built to be photographed, and a handwritten menu on every plate told guests what was coming next, including the late-night snack.
What we planned
Concept and design, installation, catering, staging and the evening schedule, with a quiet hour before the music started.

data.title: Retirement Lunch Beneath the Olives
data.summary: Forty colleagues, one long lunch and a shaded courtyard for thirty-two years of work.

gallery.caption: A menu card and olive sprig at each place.
Flowers and candles along the table.
A tall arrangement at the head of the table.

children.text: Margit retired after thirty-two years at the same school, and her colleagues wanted a lunch with room for stories rather than speeches. Olive Row Farm gave us a shaded courtyard and a set of stone arches.
We set a single long table with linen the colour of terracotta pots, passed platters rather than plated courses and left space for a microphone that went round the table instead of up to a stage.
What we planned
Venue, styling, catering, an open mic and a small gift table, plus a quiet send-off at four.

data.title: Graduation Dinner for Twelve
data.summary: A small family dinner in a garden room, with candles, napkins and one proud toast.

gallery.caption: Soft pink napkins and brass candlesticks.
A menu printed for the evening.
Velvet chairs waiting around the table.

children.text: A graduation dinner at home for the family of twelve. The garden room was small, so we kept the styling low and warm and let the candles do most of the work.
Everything arrived ready to set: linen, glassware, flowers and a menu card for every guest. We left before the first course and returned for the clear-down while the family stayed at the table.
What we planned
Table design, hire, menu and service staff for a single evening.

data.title: Engagement Party in the Orangery
data.place: The Orangery at Hallam House, Port Alder
data.summary: Peonies on a gold pedestal, peach velvet and an evening of toasts for two families.

gallery.caption: Loose garden roses by the entrance.
The centrepiece in peonies and mimosa.
A dessert table cake in warm colours.

children.text: Two families were meeting properly for the first time, and the engaged couple wanted the room to do some of the introducing. The Orangery's long windows and warm evening light helped.
We used one dramatic centrepiece, a peony-and-mimosa bowl on a gold pedestal, and kept everything else gentle: dusty-rose velvet chairs, cream linen and low candles.
What we planned
Design, florals, catering liaison, seating that mixed the families and a short programme of toasts.
